title: A cartesian source square gives a 2-cartesian square of quotient stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,j,c)$ and $(V,Q,s',t',e',j',c')$ be groupoids in algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: on every test scheme their points form groupoids, with the displayed source, target, identity, inverse and composition maps, naturally under pullback. Let $f_0:U\to V$ and $f_1:R\to Q$ commute with all these maps. Write $[U/R]$ and $[V/Q]$ for the fppf stackifications [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] of these presheaves of groupoids on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site], and $[f]:[U/R]\to[V/Q]$ for the morphism induced by $f_0,f_1$. If $(s,f_1):R\to U\times_{f_0,V,s'}Q$ is an isomorphism of algebraic spaces, then the canonical square with horizontal object maps $U\to[U/R]$, $V\to[V/Q]$ and vertical maps $f_0,[f]$ is a 2-fibre-product square. Equivalently, the canonical functor $U\to V\times_{[V/Q]}[U/R]$ is an equivalence over $V$. Here spaces are regarded as discrete fibred groupoids, and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 04ZN (lemma-criterion-fibre-product), with the induced morphism in lemma-quotient-stack-functorial.

proof.text: Put $A=[U/R]$, $D=[V/Q]$, and write $a:U\to A$, $b:V\to D$, $F=[f]$. The stackification extension property of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] supplies $F$ with the comparison $Fa\cong bf_0$, compatible with $f_1$ on arrows. In the formulas below this comparison is inserted whenever an image of a chart object or arrow is identified. By the fibrewise definition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], $B=V\times_D A$ has objects $(v,x,\alpha:b(v)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x))$. Its arrows to $(w,y,\beta)$ are an equality $v=w$ and $h:x\to y$ with $F(h)\alpha=\beta$. It is an fppf stack: glue local $v$ in the sheaf $V$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], glue local $x$ and its descent arrows in $A$, and glue the local $\alpha$ in the isomorphism sheaf of $D$. Their overlap equation is exactly the displayed arrow equation; arrows glue uniquely by the sheaf axiom in $A$. This also treats empty covers. The canonical comparison $G:U\to B$ sends $u$ to $(f_0(u),a(u),1)$; all constructions commute with pullback.

source.place: Tag 04ZN (lemma-criterion-fibre-product), direct local-object/arrow-lifting proof; stackification input: stacks.tex Tags 02ZP and 0436; local equivalence: Tag 046N.

proof.text: For $u,w\in U(T)$ the presheaf of arrows from $u$ to $w$ is $I_{u,w}(T')=\{r\in R(T'):s(r)=u|_{T'},\ t(r)=w|_{T'}\}$ on $T$-schemes. It is an fppf sheaf: glue the local $r$ uniquely in $R$, and check the endpoint equations locally in the sheaf $U$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The identical argument for $Q,V$ gives its arrow sheaves. Sheafification fixes these sheaves: the universal factorization in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of their identity gives an inverse to the unit, and uniqueness gives the other inverse identity. Consequently [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] identifies arrows between $a(u),a(w)$ with actual sections $r$ of $R$ with those endpoints, and similarly arrows between $b(v),b(z)$ with sections of $Q$. These identifications respect composition and pullback and make $F$ act by $f_1$.

source.place: Tag 04ZN (lemma-criterion-fibre-product), direct local-object/arrow-lifting proof; stackification input: stacks.tex Tags 02ZP and 0436; local equivalence: Tag 046N.

proof.text: The assumed isomorphism $(s,f_1)$ gives, on every test scheme $T$, a unique arrow $r\in R(T)$ with any prescribed $s(r)=u$ and $f_1(r)=q$ satisfying $s'(q)=f_0(u)$. In particular an arrow $G(u)\to G(w)$ in $B(T)$ requires $f_0(u)=f_0(w)$ and, by step 2, an $r:u\to w$ with $f_1(r)=e'(f_0(u))$. The identity $e(u)$ has exactly this source and image. Uniqueness forces $r=e(u)$ and hence $w=u$. Conversely when $w=u$ this identity supplies the unique arrow. Thus the map from the discrete groupoid $U(T)$ induces a bijection on every arrow set, including the empty sets: $G$ is fibrewise fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 04ZN (lemma-criterion-fibre-product), direct local-object/arrow-lifting proof; stackification input: stacks.tex Tags 02ZP and 0436; local equivalence: Tag 046N.

proof.text: For $(v,x,\alpha)\in B(T)$, [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] gives an fppf cover and, on each member, $u\in U$ with $\theta:a(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}x$. Work on one member. The composite $q=F(\theta)^{-1}\alpha:b(v)\to b(f_0(u))$ is an actual $Q$-arrow by step 2, with source $v$ and target $f_0(u)$. Apply the unique lifting of step 3 to $q^{-1}$ with source $u$. This gives $r:u\to w$ in $R$, where $w=t(r)$ and $f_0(w)=t'(q^{-1})=v$. Set $h=\theta\,a(r)^{-1}:a(w)\to x$. Since $f_1(r)=q^{-1}$, one has $F(h)=F(\theta)q=\alpha$. Therefore $(1_v,h)$ is an isomorphism $G(w)\xrightarrow{\sim}(v,x,\alpha)$ in $B$. Every object of $B$ is locally in the essential image of $G$.

source.place: Tag 04ZN (lemma-criterion-fibre-product), direct local-object/arrow-lifting proof; stackification input: stacks.tex Tags 02ZP and 0436; local equivalence: Tag 046N.

proof.text: The sheaf $U$, viewed as a discrete fibred groupoid, is an fppf stack: sections glue uniquely by its sheaf axiom, and any descent arrow is an equality. The same site and larger universe work for $U$ and $B$, by [def-pc-fppf-site] and [def-weil-size-convention]. Step 1 makes $B$ a stack, step 3 proves fibrewise full faithfulness, and step 4 proves covering-local essential surjectivity. Thus [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] applies to the pullback-compatible functor $G$ and gives an equivalence over the site. Since $G$ projects to $f_0$ on $V$ and to $a$ on $A$, it is an equivalence over $V$ and is precisely the canonical comparison to the 2-fibre product. The definition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] now identifies the asserted square as 2-cartesian.
